title: Severe Allergic Reaction (Anaphylaxis)
immediate_warning: Call 112 immediately. This is a life-threatening emergency. Use adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector if available.

description: Anaphylaxis is a severe, sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction. Common triggers include foods (groundnuts, shellfish), medications, and insect stings.

steps.instruction: If the person has an adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector (EpiPen), use it on the outer thigh immediately.

instruction_translations.en: If the person has an adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector (EpiPen), use it on the outer thigh immediately.

instruction_translations.pcm: [NEEDS_REVIEW] If the person has an adrenaline (epinephrine) auto-injector (EpiPen), use it on the outer thigh immediately.

steps.instruction: Lay the person flat with their legs elevated. If breathing is difficult, let them sit up slightly.

steps.instruction: Remove or avoid the trigger allergen if still present (e.g. remove a bee stinger).

do_not: Do not leave the person alone.
Do not give oral medication if they cannot swallow.
Do not let them stand up.
